definitions.explanation: Wheat flour with a medium protein (gluten) content, between cake flour and bread flour. Typically used for udon noodles, takoyaki, and some baked goods.

examples.japanese: {中力粉|ちゅうりきこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
⟦うどん→うどん：05182_udon⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{中力粉|ちゅうりきこ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: Udon is made with medium-gluten flour.

examples.japanese: {中力粉|ちゅうりきこ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{薄力粉|はくりきこ}→薄力粉：20705_hakurikiko⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{弾力|だんりょく}→弾力：14924_danryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{強力粉|きょうりきこ}→強力粉：20706_kyourikiko⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧やわらかい⟦{食感|しょっかん}→食感：06636_shokkan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Medium-gluten flour has more elasticity than cake flour but produces a softer texture than bread flour.

notes:
Japanese wheat flour is classified by protein content into three main grades. {中力粉|ちゅうりきこ} sits in the middle and is the standard flour for udon, somen, and similar noodles.

FLOUR GRADES:
- ⟦{薄力粉|はくりきこ}→薄力粉：20705_hakurikiko⟧: cake flour (low protein) — tempura batter, cakes, cookies
- {中力粉|ちゅうりきこ}: medium flour — udon, takoyaki, okonomiyaki
- ⟦{強力粉|きょうりきこ}→強力粉：20706_kyourikiko⟧: bread flour (high protein) — bread, pizza dough

Note that Japanese {中力粉|ちゅうりきこ} is closer in protein content to European "plain flour" than to American all-purpose flour, which is closer to a blend of ⟦{薄力粉|はくりきこ}→薄力粉：20705_hakurikiko⟧ and {中力粉|ちゅうりきこ}.
